## Objective
Unit tests (node:test, node:assert/strict) for the pure game logic in `src/logic.js`, written before the implementation. They must fail against the stub and pass against a correct implementation.

## Interface
Import `{ createState, turn, tick, placeFood }` from `../src/logic.js`. Types are documented in the stub `src/logic.js` (State, Point, Direction). `rng` is `() => number` in [0,1); tests pass deterministic ones.

## Behavior
1. createState(20,15): snake has 3 contiguous cells, head first, near the centre, direction and nextDirection 'right', score 0, status 'running', food non-null and not on the snake and inside the grid.
2. tick moves the head one cell in `direction` and drops the tail; length unchanged; input state is not mutated.
3. turn(state,'up') sets nextDirection; tick then moves up and sets direction 'up'.
4. turn to the opposite of the current direction is ignored.
5. Reversal is judged against `direction`, not `nextDirection`: moving right, turn 'up' then turn 'left' leaves nextDirection 'up'.
6. Eating: with food directly ahead, tick grows the snake by 1, score +10, new food placed off the snake.
7. Hitting a wall gives status 'over'; tick on a non-running state returns it unchanged.
8. Moving into the snake's own body gives 'over'; moving into the cell the tail is vacating is allowed.
9. placeFood never returns a snake cell; returns null when the snake fills the grid; uses rng to choose among free cells.
10. Eating that fills the whole grid gives status 'won'.

## Invariants
Tests are deterministic, no timers, no DOM, no network. Build states by hand-constructing State objects.

## Edge cases
Wall on all four sides; 2x2 or 3x1 tiny grids for the 'won' and null-food cases.

## Guardrails
Do not edit `src/logic.js`. Do not test rendering.

## Out of scope
UI, input handling, game loop.
